 Cost of living changes, payment schedules & more: What you need to know about Social Security
 Francine Frazier , Senior Digital Producer
 Published:  October 20, 2026 at 12:07 PM Tags:  Social Security , Politics , Money , Consumer , SSI , Social Security Income FILE - A Social Security card is displayed Oct. 12, 2021, in Tigard, Ore. (AP Photo/Jenny Kane, File) (Jenny Kane, Copyright 2021 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.) Social Security and Supplemental Security Income recipients will see a 3.6% cost-of-living increase in 2027, while several payments will arrive earlier than usual during the final months of 2026 because of weekends and federal holidays.
 The Social Security Administration announced the 2027 adjustment Oct. 14. It will add about $75 a month to the average retired worker’s benefit, raising it from $2,095 to $2,170, according to the agency. The increase is based on inflation measured from the third quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of 2026.
 Recommended Videos
 The larger benefit amounts begin in January. SSI recipients will receive their January payment early, on Dec. 31, because New Year’s Day falls on a federal holiday. None of the remaining regular Social Security payments in 2026 will include the increase.
 Who gets paid and when 
 For most people who started receiving Social Security after May 1997, payment dates are based on their birth date:
 Birthdays from the 1st through the 10th: second Wednesday of the month. 
 Birthdays from the 11th through the 20th: third Wednesday. 
 Birthdays from the 21st through the 31st: fourth Wednesday. 
 People who began receiving benefits before May 1997, as well as some people who receive both Social Security and SSI, generally get Social Security payments on the third of each month. If that date falls on a weekend or federal holiday, payment is made on the preceding business day.
 Remaining 2026 payment dates 
 October 
 Oct. 21: Social Security recipients with birthdays from the 11th through the 20th. 
 Oct. 28: Recipients with birthdays from the 21st through the 31st. 
 Oct. 30: November SSI payment, issued early because Nov. 1 falls on a Sunday. 
 November 
 Nov. 3: People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 and eligible recipients who receive both Social Security and SSI. 
 Nov. 10: Recipients with birthdays from the 1st through the 10th. The payment is early because Veterans Day, Nov. 11, is a federal holiday. 
 Nov. 18: Recipients with birthdays from the 11th through the 20th. 
 Nov. 25: Recipients with birthdays from the 21st through the 31st. 
 There will be no SSI payment issued in November; that month’s payment arrives Oct. 30.
 December 
 Dec. 1: December SSI payment. 
 Dec. 3: People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 and eligible recipients who receive both Social Security and SSI. 
 Dec. 9: Recipients with birthdays from the 1st through the 10th. 
 Dec. 16: Recipients with birthdays from the 11th through the 20th. 
 Dec. 23: Recipients with birthdays from the 21st through the 31st. 
 Dec. 31: January 2027 SSI payment, issued early because Jan. 1 is a federal holiday. 
 SSI payments are normally issued on the first of the month. When that date falls on a weekend or federal holiday, the payment moves to the preceding business day. That creates two SSI deposits in October and two in December, but no payment during November.
 The 2027 COLA will also raise the maximum federal SSI payment standard to $1,029 a month for an individual and $1,544 for an eligible couple. Actual benefits vary by recipient. The SSA says personalized notices with new benefit amounts will be available through my Social Security accounts beginning in late November.
